header.name: Distributed and Federated Machine Learning
header.description: This course aims to provide a deeper understanding of Distributed and Federated Machine Learning (ML) training algorithms to senior undergraduate and graduate students who already have done an introductory course in ML. The course will introduce/recapitulate the theory of convex optimization and will describe the scalable and decentralized methods of training ML models. The course will focus on both convergence theory and implementation of the algorithms to train popular ML models such as Neural Networks.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students learn the analytical aspects of a machine learning model training problem. Students will be able to understand mathematical notions such as smoothness, strict-/strong-/non- convexity, and the rate and order of convergence of an iterative algorithm.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students get familiar with the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for training machine learning models. In particular, they learn SGD variants such as RMSProp, AdaGrad, ADAM, etc. Students will be able to understand the dynamics of the optimization algorithms both analytically and geometrically.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students learn the distributed and federated implementation of SGD. Students prove the convergence of a number of well-accepted distributed and federated machine learning algorithms.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to train models, e.g. a Neural Network, using a popular distributed/federated Machine Learning framework implemented in Python/Pytorch.

lecture_topics: Introduction to convex sets and functions
Gradient Descent (GD) and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
Hyperparameters such as batch-size, learning-rate, and momentum of SGD
AdaGrad, RMSProp, ADAM, and other SGD variants
Introduction to large-scale models, such as foundation models, and training on big data
Introduction to decentralized data and federated training
Cross-silo, cross-device, vertial and horizontal federated learning
Introduction to Pytorch Distributed, FedML/OpenFL frameworks
SCAFFOLD, FedOpt, and other federated learning algorithms

resources.title: Lectures on Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Guanghui Lan, 2019
Convex Optimization, Boyd and Vandenberghe, Cambridge University Press, 2004
Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity, Sébastien Bubeck, 2015
